implementation: Added an explicit scenario runner that lists runnable and blocked acceptance cases and only runs user-selected cases; it does not start a long suite by default.

The provider-conformance acceptance scenario verifies formal external-loop timeout checkpointing and Linux worker process-group cleanup. Current-source Trainer conformance additionally exposes the runner-owned cooperative deadline and verifies finite stop-at-step-boundary behavior; a blocked Python/CUDA call still requires the process watchdog and may not checkpoint.

Existing complex-model, external-loop, independent extension, provider, and offline environment acceptance scripts are wired as runnable cases. Their scenario-level covered/uncovered scope is stated separately from overall product acceptance.

Each emitted record binds the product document version, Git HEAD plus dirty-worktree content fingerprint, runtime details, exact argv, exit code, captured logs, timestamp, and covered/uncovered scope. Generated acceptance output is excluded from the source worktree fingerprint.

Reduced repeated test-only PyTorch availability probing: the 57-test CLI binary previously spawned one `import torch` process per guarded test (50 occurrences); CLI, device and training-mode test binaries now memoize this per process. The train-device suite also memoizes GPU discovery.

The initial hard-coded edit-persistence blocker was replaced with a runnable focused acceptance wrapper after EDIT-01/02/03/05 integrations passed; the only currently blocked scenario is real target-user value validation.

Moved generated assembly file creation behind the ProjectSourceWriter port and file adapter; the application layer no longer performs filesystem writes. Synchronized run_artifact_manifest schema version 2 between Python protocol and compatibility contract.

Added a provenance-bound S-supervision acceptance scenario for manual semantic marking, batch-axis binding, read-only preview, explicit managed/manual training, pre-update mismatch rejection, and honest partial/insufficient coverage reporting. The evidence is mapped to product.json 0.13.62; full S-supervision remains partial because custom validator/penalty protocol and semantic target validation are unimplemented.

S-supervision now binds manually selected finite/range sample axis to explicitly declared stable batch envelope IDs or StepContext.report_sample_ids. Current-batch violations can be named in previews and pre-update require errors; missing/mismatched IDs are unsupported. The acceptance fixture exercises this behavior while preserving the broader partial-coverage statement.

S-supervision 0.13.59 adds per-rule multi-batch deduplication and checkpoint/resume continuity using SHA-256 ID summaries; repository acceptance proves repeated IDs are deduplicated after explicit sampler reset. Authenticity, dataset denominator and broader supervision extensions remain uncovered.

S-supervision 0.13.61 acceptance covers explicit external-loop supervision through a user-owned supervised_step/context.backward/registered-optimizer protocol, including formal checkpoint/resume and multi-batch sample evidence. Product 0.13.62 records the manual mark → target/rule binding → read-only preview → explicit mode selection flow and reconciles the delivered external-loop/deduplication behavior against remaining custom-plugin and identity/label limits.

S-supervision 0.13.63 adds current-source acceptance for project-local custom validator and differentiable-penalty callables: real read-only preview, explicit named loss contribution, and pinned source drift rejection. The plugin protocol is input/output constrained but runs as trusted in-process Python; no OS sandbox/resource budget is claimed. ID authenticity, dataset denominator and task-label semantics remain uncovered.

RUN-02 local Linux support boundary was re-verified on product 0.13.63: PTY HUP/reconnect, detached supervisor SIGKILL to unknown, checkpoint preservation and child-run recovery all pass; real SSH/network/host faults remain external evidence rather than a claimed capability.

Added a runner-owned cooperative deadline to external-loop Trainer conformance. The deadline starts at worker startup, is exposed through context.timeout_requested/remaining_time_seconds, and report_step() returns false at the first step boundary after expiry; ignoring that boundary fails with TRAINER_TIMEOUT_IGNORED. Formal CLI watchdog remains the process-level backstop.

QA-02 added a distinct environment-runtime-probe acceptance case: it exercises an explicitly selected Python interpreter with `m-model env probe --library torch --check-runtime`, verifies real CPU arithmetic and the no-auto-install/no-auto-bind policy, and records GPU/other-platform coverage as explicitly uncovered.

Current-source final QA-02 sweep: 13/13 runnable scenarios verified and 1 external human-value scenario explicitly skipped; all 14 evidence records validate against Draft 2020-12 schema with FormatChecker and share one worktree fingerprint. Evidence: docs/acceptance/results/qa02-current-tree-20261121-4/. This run occurred after the explicit inherited-system-site environment policy and same-preview E4 recovery were implemented.
